en.title: Smallest-Numbered Locker
en.description:
Lockers are numbered starting from 1, and there are always enough of them. Each time a visitor arrives: if they do not hold a locker yet, assign them the smallest currently free number; otherwise release their locker. Find the number of the last locker assigned over the whole sequence. The last event may be a release.

The input format, examples and test data were compiled and written by CSWork.
en.input: The first line contains n (1..100000), followed by n visitor identifiers. On this site, identifiers are strings of 1..32 English letters or digits with no whitespace.
en.output: Output the answer as described; multiple results are separated by spaces in order.
en.explanation: The example input and output follow the rules above directly; see the editorial for the full algorithm.
hints: Use a hash map to record the locker each visitor holds and a min-heap to store released numbers; when no number can be reused, use the next new number in increasing order.
